patch_description:
The current design applies RZ to all 8 qubits in the final layer with full parameter sharing (all use "rz_final"). This is parameter-efficient but creates over-parameterization on odd qubits which already receive rich rotations (RY in initial layer + RY in intermediate + bracketing). 

By reducing the final RZ layer to only even-indexed qubits (0, 2, 4, 6), we:
1. Drop from 6 to 5 distinct parameters, improving parameter efficiency further
2. Maintain expressivity since odd qubits still have sufficient rotation degrees of freedom earlier in the circuit
3. Reduce circuit depth and gate count, improving computational efficiency
4. Force the optimizer to rely more on earlier entangling blocks to discriminate samples, potentially improving worst-group margin through better distributed feature learning

This aligns with the principle that fewer, well-placed parameters with stronger individual impact generalize better than many redundant ones.
